title: U-Bench: A Comprehensive Understanding of U-Net through 100-Variant Benchmarking
mechanism: One protocol for 100 U-Net variants on 28 2D datasets, with paired t-tests against U-Net, a zero-shot axis (train on one dataset, test on an unseen same-modality dataset) and an accuracy-efficiency U-Score.
adaptation: Use the harness and model zoo to run 10 to 15 variants at 512 px, 1 channel, on our module-grouped folds. Test-49 is the in-domain axis and E1 the zero-shot axis. FLOPs/FPS go in as the deployment axis for WattCycle.
min_experiment: U-Net, Swin-UMamba, RWKV-UNet, MEGANet, UTANet, U-KAN and VM-UNet under one recipe, one seed per fold; rank by test crack relF1@2 and E1 relF1@2 against the house model. Kill for the score line: no variant beats the house model on E1 relF1@2 by more than 0.03.
evidence: R: over 80% of variants not significantly better than U-Net in-domain; average in-domain top-1 gain 1 to 2% IoU, zero-shot more than 3% and more often significant; fundus/nuclei (thin, local) stagnate; RWKV-UNet top-1 IoU in-domain and zero-shot, Swin-UMamba #3 zero-shot; Mamba family weaker on fine detail; blurry boundaries are the main difficulty factor.
prior_overlap: none (BRIEF: no transformer or Mamba segmenter tried)

alt_notes.adaptation: Template for the EL benchmark: paired significance tests across seeds and folds, a zero-shot column (E1 and F51), an efficiency column; pick 5-8 suite members from its families via its 2D trainers.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Benchmark design, not a score arm: run U-Bench's statistical test on existing house v PF seed results; adopt if it reproduces the BRIEF minimum detectable difference (~0.012 crack IoU).
